absent: Owner identity comparison, blocker wakeup, lock allocation and freeing behavior beyond the call sites shown.
Complete layouts of file lock, nameidata, dentry, mount, open flags and binprm structures.
Temporary-file, path-only, symlink-follow, dot handling, mount traversal and final open steps beyond the dispatched names.
Permission, security hook, idmap mapping and write-access denial internals.
Dcache collection predicates, kill/dispose mechanics, submount detach and rename-lock implementation.
Exec personality, memory layout selection, credential guard and address-space teardown internals.

findings.text: Exec finalization for current task selects mapping layout, applies architecture setup, publishes address space size, releases exec ordering protection, then drops prior address space reference with resource accounting and ownership update.
Stack limit finalization copies requested stack resource value from exec parameter block into current signal state while holding group leader task protection.
Interpreter and executable opening reuses a cached loader file when present, otherwise opens the named path through an exec-oriented open helper rooted at current working directory context.

Exec open accepts only a narrow set of address-family style control flags, uses read-only large-file exec intent with execute access and open plus follow lookup behavior, rejects noexec paths and non-regular results, and requires write denial before success.

File open by directory descriptor and pathname establishes nested lookup state, tries optimistic read-side lookup first, then falls back to blocking lookup and to revalidating lookup on designated retry errors, then restores previous lookup state.

Lookup state carries inline stack storage with depth, directory descriptor, filename pointer, textual pathname, current path, saved parent pointer, root override with state flags, sequence values and traversal flags, chained through current task context.

Single lookup attempt allocates an empty file then dispatches among temporary-file creation, path-only handling, and full pathname walk loop ending in open; success requires opened mode, otherwise the file is closed and a stale error is remapped according to read-side mode.

Path walking skips repeated separators, checks traversal permission at each directory, classifies dot entries, pushes nested symlink names on a stack, steps into normal components, and captures directory ownership and mode at the final component.

Traversal permission check runs first in current lookup mode; on failure in read-side mode it attempts conversion to blocking mode and distinguishes hard denial from transient retry before a final blocking check.

Directory execute permission fast path requires directory type and restricted flag mask, then consults filesystem fast-permission capability plus restrictive mode and access-control state before delegating to full permission evaluation and security hook.

Fast dentry lookup in read-side mode validates parent sequence after cache lookup and honors revalidation outcome; on miss or revalidation request it converts to blocking mode and may repeat revalidation before accepting, invalidating or failing.

Conversion from read-side to blocking walk legitimizes saved links, current path and grabbed root; any failure drops link state, clears current path identity, exits read-side protection and reports inability to continue optimistically.

Mount legitimization samples mount generation, takes a mount reference with an ordering barrier, rechecks generation, and on change serializes on mount hash to detect synchronous unmount or doomed state before deciding success or retry.

Walk termination in blocking mode releases current path, stacked link paths and grabbed root, while in read-side mode it only exits read-side protection; depth and current path identity are then reset and delayed link actions are run on pop.
Global lock insertion asserts global file semaphore protection, records the inserting processor identity, and prepends the entry to the local processor list under that list lock.
Global lock removal asserts the same semaphore protection, skips already unlinked entries, otherwise locks the originating processor list recorded at insertion and removes plus reinitializes linkage.

Context detach removes global registration, reinitializes list membership and wakes blockers; context delete then either queues the core entry onto a caller disposal list or frees its enclosing lock object.
Range overlap means each interval end reaches the other start; type conflict means either side requests exclusivity; POSIX conflict additionally requires distinct ownership and overlapping ranges.
Unlock classification inspects the core lock type in one build variant and is a constant negative in another variant, showing configuration-dependent availability of unlock state.

Deadlock detection follows ultimate-blocker chains through an owner hash, bounded by an iteration cap; description-based locks never report deadlock, and encountering the original owner reports a cycle.
Deadlock chain traversal requires the blocked-waiter protection to be held, enforced by an assertion at entry.

Dentry invalidation drops hash identity under dentry lock, returns early when already unhashed or without inode, otherwise shrinks the subtree and loops detaching submounts until none remain, with a final shrink if any were found.

Tree walking serializes against rename generation with a retry loop, nests child locks under parent locks, honors visitor continue, quit, skip and no-retry directives, and revalidates ancestry when ascending.

Dcache shrinking repeatedly collects reclaimable dentries by tree walk, disposes each batch, yields execution, then either waits for completion of a dying victim or directly kills a live victim before disposing again.
Dentry waiter registration refuses already killed dentries and otherwise initializes completion state and pushes the waiter onto the dentry waiter chain.
Small filesystem helpers expose file reference reading, inode write-count release on non-null files, and executable write restoration that skips null files and special notify mode.
Exec open intent combines large-file, read-only and exec behavior with execute access and open plus follow lookup semantics; only nofollow, empty-path and execve-check control flags are accepted.
Lock classification distinguishes exclusive, shared and unlock types, and a dedicated open-file-description flag selects non-process ownership semantics that bypass deadlock detection.
Optimistic lookup staleness surfaces as redoable errors that require outer retry in blocking or revalidating mode; failed revalidation invalidates the dentry and drops its reference.
Exec open treats a post-lookup non-regular result as a one-time warning and access failure, closing the write-denial window against filesystem type races.
